source.title: Repeated Shared Access Enables Grokking, but Edit Propagation Depends on an Addressable Memory

page_placements.theme: Architecture, initialization and objective control the delay

record.tranche_reason: Tests delayed OOD generalization in a synthetic knowledge-graph QA setting, extending grokking beyond the classic small algorithmic-task setting; it measures threshold-crossing times under different shared-access architectures.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own OOD grokking onset results for KG-QA configurations, which bear on V1. It does not report training-accuracy saturation or a training-set-size sweep. Editing, localization, and OpenWebText results do not measure the grokking behavior in the claim versions; cited findings from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper uses grokking, taken from Wang et al.'s KG-QA recipe, as a binary learning metric: the first step at which OOD 2-hop accuracy exceeds 0.1. It uses that metric to compare architectures, and its main question is edit propagation. It reports no training-accuracy curve, so it never shows OOD generalization arriving long after training saturation. It explicitly avoids a near-perfect endpoint criterion and runs no training-set-size sweep. Its onset steps therefore cannot show V1's delay. They are architecture-performance measurements, and the architecture dependence is recorded under fits_no_version. No other version is addressed by its own results.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but incomplete. The authors' headline conclusion is a dissociation. Repeated shared access (loop recomputation or memory rereading) suffices to cross the OOD grokking barrier that Dense fails, and at matched scale the loop route reaches onset faster. Edit propagation, by contrast, depends on an addressable memory site: both memory-bearing cells propagate strongly (LMC 0.78–0.92, Dense+Mem 0.71–0.96), Loop only weakly (0.04–0.30) and Dense near zero (0.00–0.03). They disclaim generalization to natural-language pretraining or RAG.
record.recipe_differences: Uses synthetic KG-QA and held-out OOD two-hop compositions rather than the classic small algorithmic datasets; defines onset as the first step OOD accuracy exceeds 0.1 and compares loop and shared-memory architectures. The paper says its task and grokking recipe follow Wang et al. [1].
record.method_sensitivity: OOD onset varies with architecture/shared-access route, memory access count, and scale-matching: one memory access fails while two or more cross the threshold; in the scale-matched comparison Loop-Iso reaches onset sooner than DenseMem-Iso.

fits_no_version.finding: In the synthetic KG-QA task (12 effective layers), dense no-memory models never cross OOD>0.1 within 5×10^6 steps (0/5 seeds). Every configuration with repeated shared access crosses on 5/5 seeds (45k–245k steps). One memory access fails; two or more succeed (about 165k). At matched scale, the loop route reaches onset faster than the dense-memory route (146k vs 449k, p=0.008).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether and when delayed OOD compositional generalization (grokking onset) occurs depends on architecture: it requires repeated access to a shared substrate, either recurrence or repeated memory reads.

record.code_released: not stated (the text says an anonymized repository will accompany submission and be de-anonymized on acceptance)
record.problems: Five seeds per configuration. The grokking measure is an onset threshold of OOD accuracy > 0.1, not a reported trajectory showing training accuracy saturated at perfect accuracy while test accuracy stayed at chance, nor a near-perfect test-accuracy endpoint. No training-set-size sweep is reported. The study itself states that its synthetic controlled design does not establish generalization to natural-language pretraining or RAG systems.
record.rows_left_out: No grokking-related results left out. Editing/localization interventions and OpenWebText perplexity results were excluded because they do not measure the grokking behavior named in the claim versions; citations to other studies were also excluded.

untested.parts: Training-accuracy saturation before OOD rise; jump to near-perfect test accuracy (final LMC OOD is about 0.81); dependence of delay on training-set size; classic algorithmic tasks.
No progress measures across training or circuit-formation dynamics; lesions are on final checkpoints only.
Not addressed (the OpenWebText runs report perplexity only).
Not addressed (weight decay is fixed at 0.1; no dataset-size sweep).
Not addressed; authors disclaim shared circuits across routes.
Not addressed (AdamW and bfloat16 are fixed).

record.verdict_notes: Grokking here is operationalized as an onset threshold (OOD>0.1, about 25× chance), and the authors state they do not use saturation or final values. Training-accuracy curves are never reported, so the defining delay of V1 cannot be assessed from this paper. The architecture dependence of KG-QA grokking was already reported by Wang et al. [1].

versions.untested_parts: Tests OOD grokking onset in synthetic KG-QA, but not whether training accuracy first saturates while test accuracy is at chance, whether test accuracy ultimately becomes near-perfect, or whether shrinking the training set increases the delay. The tested models are not classic modular-arithmetic algorithmic-task models.
Does not test gradual formation of a generalizing circuit, later removal of memorizing components, or continuous mechanistic progress measures.
Does not test non-algorithmic image, text, or molecule data, nor switching grokking through initialization scale or weight norm.
Does not test delayed generalization during realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning.
Does not test whether weight decay or low-norm bias causes an efficient generalizing circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below it.
Does not identify or compare the algorithms learned across runs.
Does not test whether optimizer or numerical artifacts cause the delay or whether controlling them removes it.

relation.reason: The operational endpoint is first OOD accuracy above 0.1, without a measured delay relative to training saturation, near-perfect generalization, or another direct test of a catalog claim version.

tranche.reason: Uses an OOD threshold-crossing metric to compare learning routes and establish models for edit-propagation experiments; it does not measure the delayed-generalization behavior specified by the catalog versions.

source_check.notes: All 25 listed rows match Table 9. Threshold crossing establishes above-chance OOD onset; it does not establish the full grokking trajectory described by V1.

statements.correction: Tables 2 and 9: all configurations have 12 effective layers; Dense crosses on 0/5 seeds; the five shared-access configurations each cross on 5/5 seeds, with onsets spanning 45k–245k. Table 7: maximum training budget up to 5×10^6 steps, stopping at grokking or convergence. §3.1: same-scale Loop-Iso onsets 140k–155k; DenseMem-Iso onsets 310k–640k.
statements.problem: The 45k–245k range covers the configurations in Table 9, not every repeated-shared-access configuration at 12 effective layers. The same-scale controls in §3.1 include DenseMem-Iso onsets of 310k–640k.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Shared-access KG-QA configurations that cross the OOD threshold
reader_labels.reason: All five seeds of the shared-FFN memory, partial-sharing loop, Loop, Dense+Mem, and LMC configurations cross the stated OOD onset threshold; see r06–r30. The evidence supports delayed OOD onset in this setting, not all components of V1.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The dense anchor stays below the OOD threshold in all five seeds, while the shared-access configurations cross it; see r01–r05 and r06–r30.
